title: CLF Stock Hits Buy Signal as Steelmaker Projects $4 Billion Outlook – Investor’s Business Daily
body:
The shares of Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. (NYSE: CLF) surged on Tuesday after the iron‑ore miner‑turned‑steelmaker unveiled a bullish outlook that projects roughly $4 billion in EBITDA by the end of 2027. The guidance, coupled with the company’s first full‑year profit in more than a decade, ignited a technical “buy” signal on several charting platforms and sent the stock climbing more than 12 percent in early trading. Investors are now weighing whether the ambitious earnings forecast reflects a sustainable turnaround or a short‑term market rally driven by higher commodity prices.

Cleveland-Cliffs, historically known for its bulk‑commodity mining operations, has been on a strategic overhaul since 2020, when it announced plans to integrate downstream steel production into its business model. The acquisition of AK Steel in 2020 and the purchase of a majority stake in ArcelorMittal USA’s former blast furnaces in 2021 were intended to capture more value from the steel value chain. After a painful restructuring period marked by plant closures and workforce reductions, the company finally reported a net profit of $85 million for 2023, reversing a string of losses that dated back to 2015.

The $4 billion EBITDA target hinges on several assumptions: a sustained uplift in steel demand from the construction and automotive sectors, a gradual easing of raw‑material cost pressures, and the successful ramp‑up of the newly acquired U.S. steel facilities. Analysts at major brokerages note that the outlook assumes an average steel price of $1,200 per metric ton—still above the current market level but within the range of recent peaks. If global economic growth continues to rebound, especially in emerging markets that consume the bulk of steel, the forecast could prove realistic. However, the industry remains vulnerable to macro‑economic headwinds, trade policy shifts, and the ongoing transition toward greener production methods, which could raise compliance costs and alter demand patterns.

From a valuation standpoint, the stock’s price‑to‑earnings multiple has narrowed dramatically, moving from an elevated 45‑times forward earnings in early 2023 to roughly 18‑times based on the latest earnings estimate. This compression reflects both the improved earnings outlook and a broader market correction in cyclical industrial stocks. Yet, some investors remain cautious, pointing to the company’s still‑high debt load—approximately $6 billion in long‑term obligations—and the need for continued cash flow generation to service that debt without compromising capital expenditures on modernization and emissions‑reduction initiatives.

The technical “buy” signal cited by chart analysts stems from a breakout above the 50‑day moving average, accompanied by increasing volume and a bullish relative strength index. While such indicators can attract momentum traders, seasoned market participants emphasize that technical patterns should be corroborated by fundamentals. In Cleveland-Cliffs’ case, the convergence of a solid profit turnaround, a clear strategic vision, and a quantifiable earnings target provides a stronger foundation than the chart alone.

Looking ahead, the company’s ability to meet its 2027 EBITDA goal will depend on execution across several fronts: maintaining operational efficiency at its integrated steel mills, navigating volatile raw‑material costs, and investing in low‑carbon technologies to meet tightening environmental regulations. If Cleveland-Cliffs can deliver on these fronts, the stock could continue its upward trajectory and potentially become a bellwether for the broader U.S. steel industry’s resurgence. Conversely, any misstep—whether a slowdown in steel demand or an unexpected cost surge—could erode the gains and reignite skepticism. Investors will be watching the next quarterly report closely for clues on whether the $4 billion vision is a realistic milestone or an aspirational target still out of reach.
